text: Tobecome a freelancer in Germany, you must know how much you should charge. This guide helps you set your rates as a freelance software developer in Berlin.

title: Expenses and taxes
text: When you are self-employed, you must pay for your workspace, equipment, insurance, etc. Your employer does not help you. Those business expenses aretax-deductible. You also pay more for health insurance, because your employer does not pay half of it. How taxes work Think about these costs: Income tax–Tax calculatorYou will pay 8% to 42% of your salary as income tax (Einkommensteuer). Income tax is the same for employees and freelancers. Health insurance–Health insurance calculatorIf you were an employee, your employer would pay half of your contribution. As a freelancer, you pay it alone. This means your health insurance will cost you twice as much. Since public health insurance costs a percentage of your salary, it can get very expensive. Private health insurance charges according on your health condition, so it can be much cheaper if you are young. –More information. Liability insurance(optional)If you make an expensive mistake, liability insurance covers for reparations and other legal costs. Personal liability insurance does not cover your business activities. You need a professional liability insurance. –More information Trade taxIf you are aGewerbe, you must pay trade tax (Gewerbesteuer). In Berlin, the costs an extra 14.35% of allprofitabove €24,500. –More information VATYou must charge VAT on your products and services, and give that money to theFinanzamt. If you are aKleinunternehmer, you can decide to charge VAT, but you don’t have to. –More information Pension and savingsYou must save some money for emergencies, and for retirement. As a freelancer, you don’t haveunemployment insurance, and you don’t automatically makepublic pensionpayments. If you lose your income, you get nothing. You must prepare for this. Office space, equipment, software.You will need to use your own equipment. You might also want to rent a co-working space. If you were an employee, your employer would pay for those. You must include these costs in your calculations. Finances and bookkeepingYou must pay for bookkeeping and invoicing software, and for a business bank account. This costsat least€20to €50per month. You might need a tax advisor (Steuerberater) to help you with your taxes. Usethis calculatorto estimate the cost of a tax advisor. Thecost of living in BerlinYou must make enough money to live in Berlin. Thecost of living in Berlincan be different from what you are used to. You could need more money (or less) to have the same lifestyle. How to start a business in Germany

title: No paid vacations
text: As a freelancer, you don’t havepaid vacations,paid holidaysorsick days. When you don’t work, you don’t get paid. If you remove the weekends, the national holidays and 30 vacation days, will only work around 210 days per year.1Think about this when you set your rates. You don’t always get paid to work. The time you spend finding clients, doing your taxes or updating your website is not billable.

title: Lower rates for long contracts
text: You usually charge more per hour for short contracts, and less for longer contracts. Longer contracts are more stable, and have less overhead. You spend less time finding clients, interviewing, writing contracts, etc.

title: Most developers charge by the day
text: Most software developers have a daily rate. They charge for each full day of work. They rarely charge per hour, or per project.

title: VAT is not included
text: If you say that you charge €500per day, your client will expect to pay €500per day plus 19% for theVAT.2
